decisions.statement: A filesystem held in memory is read from what the kernel says is mounted.
Which filesystems those are is read rather than named here.
A write landing under one of those mounts is refused.
A byte written there is memory the fleet has back only once the file goes.
A removal is let through, because a removal is what gives the memory back.
The refusal names the mount rather than the path alone.
The refusal names where scratch goes instead.
A payload this cannot read judges nothing and exits so the dispatch refuses.
What a shell write is comes from the hook guarding akasha's own folder.
A path named only inside a program handed to an interpreter is not seen.
A mount made after this call began is not seen by this call.

definition: the hook refusing a shell write onto a filesystem the machine holds in memory
